episode_title: 221. Can You Use ChatGPT for Divorce Advice? What to Verify Before You Trust an AI Answer

real_qa.q: What did the Cordell & Cordell survey reveal about AI-generated divorce content being sent to family lawyers?
real_qa.r: One national family law firm, Cordell & Cordell, surveyed 133 of its attorneys in spring. Eighty percent said clients had sent them correspondence, draft pleadings, or strategy ideas that the lawyers believed were generated by AI.
real_qa.requete: Cordell Cordell survey AI divorce attorneys

real_qa.q: Why did a judge deny a father's motion to dismiss a custody case based on AI-provided legal reasoning about state jurisdiction?
real_qa.r: The father used AI during a custody case in another state. AI pointed him to a general rule about which state decides custody and he wrote arguing the court did not have authority. The judge told him that's not how it works because the rule has exceptions, including emergencies, and he had filed an emergency request himself. AI gave him the basics but not how the law is actually applied.
real_qa.requete: AI custody case jurisdiction exceptions emergency

real_qa.q: How many family law rulings have judges flagged for containing fake AI citations or apparent AI mistakes?
real_qa.r: A law professor who tracks AI errors in court cases has counted 148 family law rulings where judges flagged fake citations or other apparent AI mistakes. More than a hundred of those came just this year.
real_qa.requete: 148 family law rulings fake AI citations

real_qa.q: What was the outcome for a spousal support case where AI advised a business owner that reducing payments would be easy to win?
real_qa.r: A man who owned an online wellness company asked AI whether a judge would reduce his spousal support payments based on lower business income. The chatbot said it would be easy to win, but never asked for financial documents or analyzed that his spending had not gone down. The request was filed, the other side used the same records to argue income had not dropped, the judge agreed after a year, and a forensic accountant later found incomplete accounting of spoiled products. It took two law firms and nearly two years to resolve what AI described as easy, and he likely overpaid support the entire time.
real_qa.requete: spousal support AI easy reduce payments business

real_qa.q: What specific recommendations do divorce professionals suggest for using AI responsibly during a divorce?
real_qa.r: Use AI to learn terms and understand language, build a list of questions for your attorney and financial professionals, organize your thoughts or create a checklist of documents. Do not use it to decide your strategy, do not send anything it writes to your spouse, the other attorney or the court without your attorney reviewing it first, and do not let it tell you what your numbers mean because it has not seen your numbers. If you have used AI, disclose that to your attorney or financial professionals so they understand what you have been reading.
real_qa.requete: how to use AI responsibly during divorce
